coverage.notes: Eight four-year English-taught bachelor-level programmes enumerated across the accessible campus admissions list and internally labelled 2026–27 study guide. University advertises Fall 2027 admissions but a definitive Fall 2027 programme-by-programme catalogue was not accessible, so completeness is conservatively false. Excludes master degrees and non-degree premedical track. Older legacy programme pages and 2026–27 catalogue were fully read; modern-site replacement pages were indexed but not retrievable for full-page verification.

institution.summary: AUB twin campus in Pafos, Cyprus, offering English-taught four-year degrees through three faculties.

programmes.name: Bachelor of Arts in Philosophy, Politics, and Economics
programmes.about: An interdisciplinary BA combining philosophy, politics and economics to analyse institutions, public policy and contested social questions.
programmes.overview: Students take foundational courses in political thought, economic theory and normative philosophy, then connect the three disciplines through focused PPE courses. The curriculum covers issues including economic justice, conflict and political economy, and develops quantitative and qualitative research skills. Students complete a cross-disciplinary dissertation supported by advisers. The university describes the degree as preparation for further study in social sciences and public-facing or organisational work.

programmes.name: Bachelor of Arts in Global Liberal Arts
programmes.about: An interdisciplinary liberal arts BA bringing humanities, social sciences and science together to examine global challenges from Cyprus.
programmes.overview: The core introduces influential texts, ideas and methods of inquiry across the humanities, social sciences and science. Students explore connections between social values, sustainability, place and identity, with the option to follow thematic elective areas. The programme uses discussion, close reading, reflective writing and a digital portfolio, and it draws on its Pafos setting for place-based learning. Its broad research and communication training can support postgraduate study or work across different sectors.

programmes.name: Bachelor of Business Administration in Digital Marketing
programmes.about: A business degree focused on digital campaigns, consumer behaviour, branding and evidence-based marketing decisions.
programmes.overview: Students build a foundation in business, analytics, communication and ethical decision-making before specialising in digital marketing. The curriculum addresses brand and content development, search and display advertising, social media, website optimisation and customer engagement. Practical work includes measuring campaign performance and interpreting marketing data across digital channels. General education subjects broaden the business focus, and the programme includes an additional summer term within its four-year structure.

programmes.name: Bachelor of Business Administration in Management
programmes.about: A broad business degree covering management, quantitative analysis, leadership and responsible organisational decision-making.
programmes.overview: Students study core areas such as accounting, operations, finance, marketing and business analytics alongside a liberal arts general education component. Management-focused courses develop understanding of organisational behaviour, strategic choices, teamwork and leadership. The curriculum also addresses business ethics and communication, using analytical and practical approaches to decisions within organisations. Graduates are prepared for entry-level business functions or further study in related fields.

programmes.name: Bachelor of Science in Civil Engineering and Sustainable Design
programmes.about: A civil engineering degree centred on planning, designing and managing infrastructure with sustainability and professional ethics in view.
programmes.overview: Students learn the engineering principles used to plan, design, construct and manage built-environment projects. The listed curriculum includes structural mechanics, engineering drawings and building-information modelling, hydraulics, sustainable materials and environmental topics. Mathematical and scientific foundations support design decisions, alongside work on safety, societal impact and professional responsibility. The four-year plan includes a third-year summer term and a capstone project; the catalogue describes potential progression into engineering practice or advanced study.

programmes.name: Bachelor of Science in Computer Science and Engineering
programmes.about: A computing and engineering degree combining programming, algorithms, computer systems and hardware–software integration.
programmes.overview: The programme combines computer science theory with practical engineering of computing systems. Students develop foundations in programming, data structures, algorithms, logic and mathematics, then study hardware, system architecture and engineering design. Laboratory and project activities develop implementation, testing and communication skills, with attention to ethical and sustainable technology decisions. The curriculum is designed for work across software, hardware and systems engineering or for further technical study.

programmes.name: Bachelor of Science in Industrial Engineering
programmes.about: An engineering degree about improving production, service systems and organisational processes through quantitative analysis.
programmes.overview: Students combine engineering and mathematical foundations with statistics, operations research, ergonomics, management and economics. The curriculum examines production systems, engineering management and resource allocation, including how to analyse and improve complex processes. Practical training with an organisation takes place during an eight-week summer term in the third year. Graduates can apply these methods in manufacturing or services and may pursue further industrial engineering studies.

programmes.name: Bachelor of Science in Psychology
programmes.about: A scientific psychology degree studying behaviour, cognition and development while building skills in research and analysis.
programmes.overview: The degree approaches human behaviour and mental processes as subjects for empirical investigation. Core study covers areas such as social and personality psychology, development, cognition, neuroscience and psychological problems. Students learn research design, statistical analysis, ethical practice and the interpretation and communication of evidence. This provides a basis for further psychology study and for roles where analysis of behaviour and research skills are useful; regulated clinical practice may require postgraduate qualifications.

claims.statement: The full International Baccalaureate Diploma is explicitly named as a recognised basis for applying after twelve years of school. Admission is competitive, not automatic: an entrance-test route is required, and an offer depends on successful completion of secondary school and proof of the diploma before registration. No minimum overall IB total, HL point total or core-point rule is published in the reviewed material.
